Explain the example for remove only your handler

blocks.text: Event namespaces let you label handlers for later cleanup. off can remove just the handlers with that label.
Use a local HTML page that loads jQuery 3.7 before these scripts. Examples need that library; the plain playground does not include it. Put the script after the example markup.

blocks.title: Remove only your handler

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `off` removes matching jQuery handlers. A namespace lets you remove your feature's handler without removing unrelated ones.

blocks.text: The final line removes this feature's click handler while leaving differently named handlers alone.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Calling off("click") removes all click handlers attached through jQuery on that selection. Be precise.
